sentences.en: In the evening, my friend and I went to a restaurant together and ordered a lot of dishes.

t: to pay the bill (at a restaurant)
sentences.en: After we finished eating, we called the waiter over to pay the bill.
My friend wanted to pay, and I wanted to pay too — we both wanted to treat.

t: to rush to do something first
sentences.en: The waiter had just said how much it was when I jumped in: "This one's on me!"
My friend also wanted to pay and said: "No way — today it should be me treating."
I grabbed the money, ran over to the waiter, and handed it to her first.
Once we were outside the restaurant, my friend said: "Then let me buy you a cup of coffee!"

vocab: to pay the bill (at a restaurant)
to rush to do something first

quiz.q: What did both the narrator and the friend want to do when the bill came?
a: Both wanted to leave right away
Both wanted to order more food

quiz.q: How did the narrator manage to pay first?
a: By asking the friend to wait outside
By rushing to the waiter with the money before the friend could

quiz.q: What did the friend do after losing the race to pay?
a: Offered to buy the narrator a coffee instead
Asked the waiter for a receipt

grammar.p: 抢着 + verb (to rush to be the one who does it)
grammar.e: 抢 means 'to grab/rush', and 抢着 + verb shows someone hurrying to do something before anyone else can.
grammar.x: 我就抢着说：“这次我请客！”— I jumped in: "This one's on me!"

grammar.p: 还没 A，已经 B (before A happened, B already had)
grammar.e: 还没 + verb pairs with 已经 + verb to show one thing beat another to happen.
grammar.x: 朋友还没走到，我已经把钱给了服务员。— Before my friend could get there, I had already handed the money to the waiter.

grammar.e: 那 at the start of a sentence means 'in that case' or 'then', responding to what just happened.
grammar.x: 那我请你喝一杯咖啡吧！— Then let me buy you a cup of coffee!
